video_title: Ziquidated after putting my Net Worth into Zcash.
gist: Taiki Maeda recounts being forced out of his leveraged Zcash perp long on Variational (locking ~$2.3–2.5M after being up ~$6.4M), now mostly in cash with spot ZEC, HYPE and BTC. He argues the Tachyon upgrade (shielded pool plus post-quantum opcodes, targeted for late January) rather than privacy is Zcash's real driver, predicts new highs above $2,000, and frames a Bitcoin 'crisis of confidence' in which flows rotate from BTC, ETH and SOL into Zcash, while he keeps farming perp DEX airdrops.

themes.theme: Zcash leveraged long: liquidation and positioning

insights.claim: Taiki Maeda was forced to close his leveraged Zcash perp long on Variational when Zcash broke down from a roughly $1,100–$1,400 range, locking in roughly $2.3–2.5M of profit after having been up about $6.4M at the peak.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: A large, publicly followed ZEC leverage position has been flushed; perp-driven reflexive upside is reduced near term until leverage rebuilds.
insights.quote: at the top I was like up 6.4 mil total. Um, so I did round trip a bunch.

insights.claim: After the liquidation Maeda holds no leverage and is mostly in cash, with remaining spot exposure in Zcash, Hyperliquid (HYPE) and Bitcoin, having sold his Lighter (LIT) at about $305.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Signals a de-risked stance from a prominent ZEC bull; dry powder is being held for a potential capitulation event or the Tachyon catalyst.
insights.quote: My portfolio is like roughly this, so no leverage right now. Um, so like mostly in cash.

insights.claim: Maeda defends round-tripping roughly half his peak gains by arguing the high risk tolerance and conviction needed to reach multi-million profits is inseparable from large drawdowns, and he prefers that outcome to a low-risk trade making a few hundred thousand.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Position-sizing philosophy: concentrated, levered conviction bets require accepting large drawdowns; size stops accordingly.

insights.claim: Maeda says he ignored a top signal when, at an October 8 Coinbase trading event in Singapore, a fan brought a printed meme image of him to sign and screamed 'Zcash $50,000' into the camera, after which Zcash continued lower.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Retail euphoria and personality-cult behavior around an asset are sentiment top signals worth trimming into.
insights.quote: when the universe is sending you signals maybe you should you know take some chips off the table

insights.claim: Maeda plans to re-add Zcash perp longs aggressively around December–January ahead of the Tachyon upgrade rather than now, treating 'not being in a position' as a valid position in the interim.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Watch for renewed leverage/open-interest build in ZEC from December into the January Tachyon release.
insights.quote: sometimes right like not being in a position is a position

themes.theme: Tachyon as the real Zcash catalyst

insights.claim: Maeda predicts Zcash will make new highs above $2,000 next year if not this year and rejects the idea that the ~$1,600 top is permanent after a decade-long range.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Defines his price target and timeframe; he frames ZEC at $1,100–1,400 as a buy zone ahead of the catalyst.
insights.quote: my bet is that Zcash will hit new highs above $2,000 um, next year, if not this year.

insights.claim: According to Zcash developer ZK Dragon's November 9 post, the goal for January 2027 is to release the Tachyon shielded pool and add post-quantum transparent opcodes, starting Zcash's scaling path from about 200 shielded TPS to roughly 2,000 by end of next year and eventually 50k TPS.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Hard-dated catalyst (late January) to calendar; slippage in the ship date would undercut the trade timing.
insights.quote: release the Tachon shielded pool and add postquantum transparent op codes

insights.claim: Maeda argues quantum resistance cannot be addressed without scalability because post-quantum signatures are an order of magnitude larger, so a chain that only adds post-quantum cryptography suffers bloat; he believes Bitcoin will struggle to do both in a timely way while Zcash is shipping both.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Frames the quantum threat as a relative-value trade: long chains with credible PQ+scaling roadmaps vs. Bitcoin.
insights.quote: you can't really address quantum without addressing scalability because postquantum cryptographic signatures are going to be an order of magnitude larger

insights.claim: Maeda contends Zcash's outperformance began when Tachyon lead developer Shambo published the Tachyon blog post on April 2, 2025, around Zcash's bottom, implying Tachyon rather than the privacy narrative is the true driver of the rally.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: If correct, ZEC's bid is more durable than a 'privacy pump and dump'; if wrong, the rally is narrative-dependent.
insights.quote: the real reason Zcash has been going up is not because of the privacy narrative

insights.claim: Maeda reports that fund managers with sizable capital who own Zcash could not explain what Tachyon is, which he sees as a knowledge gap that is both a source of edge and a reason momentum holders capitulate on drawdowns.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: An information gap among holders suggests repricing once the upgrade ships, but also weak hands during dips.
insights.quote: these are fund managers like managing like you know pretty sizable amounts of capital and they're like what the hell is Tachon, right?

insights.claim: Maeda frames Zcash as the most reflexive asset in crypto because its privacy set improves as more coins are shielded and price rises, so the product gets better as price goes up and worse as it falls.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Expect outsized volatility in both directions; size positions for reflexive drawdowns.
insights.quote: as price goes up, the product gets better. Um and as price goes down, the product gets worse.

themes.theme: Catalyst timing: buy the rumor ~2 months out

insights.claim: Maeda's rule of thumb is that in crypto smart money accumulates 6 to 8 weeks before a protocol event, so buyers a week before are likely exit liquidity, and about 90% of crypto events are sell-the-news unless the catalyst is genuinely bullish.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Enter catalyst trades ~2 months before the event and plan exits around the event date.
insights.quote: smart money buys these things 6 to 8 weeks before the event to dump on you

insights.claim: Maeda cites Kinetiq launching its Hyperliquid layer 2 on November 9 with its coin bottoming in August–September, and LayerZero bottoming in August ahead of a rumored October chain launch, both outperforming Bitcoin from the bottom.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Historical pattern supporting early positioning ahead of chain/protocol launches.

insights.claim: Maeda notes that Zcash's previous protocol upgrade, Ironwood on July 28, coincided with the price bottom near $450, after which Zcash went vertical from about $500 to $1,600 when Bitcoin rallied from 60K to 80K.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Precedent that buying Zcash upgrades has worked when combined with a turn in Bitcoin regime.
insights.quote: when Bitcoin went from 60 to 80K, that's when Zcash went vertical, right, from like 500 to like 1,600

insights.claim: Maeda's controversial thesis is that Bitcoin could trade like Ethereum did last cycle, failing to make meaningful new highs and ranging around $70K–$100K for the next couple of years as holders lose faith.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Argues against blind four-year-cycle assumptions; favors relative-value positioning over beta to BTC.
insights.quote: I wouldn't be surprised if Bitcoin trades between like 70 to 100K for like the next couple of years.

insights.claim: Maeda expects Ethereum to range between roughly $2K and $3K for the next five years and considers it an asset to ignore.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Continued bearish view on ETH as a long-term hold; candidate funding source for rotation into other assets.
insights.quote: I kind of expect ETH to range between like maybe 2K to 3K for like the next 5 years

insights.claim: Maeda points to underwhelming Bitcoin-to-gold and Bitcoin-to-S&P ratios, Strategy CFO Andrew King resigning, Strategy's delisting from MSCI indices, weak future cash projections, and OG Bitcoiners like Matthew Kratter turning on Michael Saylor's STRC 'digital credit' as evidence of a Bitcoin crisis of confidence.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Strategy/MSTR-related stress is a watch item for Bitcoin flows and sentiment.
insights.quote: Bitcoin to gold ratio been very very underwhelming

insights.claim: Maeda states he is bullish Zcash and holds Bitcoin as a hedge to his Zcash position, inverting the usual framing of Zcash as a hedge to Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Illustrates a ZEC-centric portfolio construction where BTC is the defensive leg.
insights.quote: Bitcoin is kind of a hedge to my Zcash position

themes.theme: Rotation into Zcash and alternate stores of value

insights.claim: Maeda predicts that over the next one to two years Bitcoiners will 'silent quit' and hedge with Zcash, capital allocators that would have full-ported Bitcoin will move toward something like 80% Bitcoin / 20% Zcash, and smart developers (e.g., ZK Dragon from Cosmos) will migrate to Zcash.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Track developer migration and allocator commentary as leading indicators of ZEC flows.
insights.quote: they might be like 80% Bitcoin, 20% Zcash or something along those lines

insights.claim: Maeda argues Zcash does not need large new inflows to crypto to rally because flows can rotate out of overvalued assets like Ethereum and Solana into Zcash.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: ZEC can outperform even in a flat or shrinking crypto liquidity environment; a pair-trade setup vs. ETH/SOL.

insights.claim: Maeda predicts the Zcash-versus-Bitcoin trade over the next couple of years will resemble Solana-versus-Ethereum last cycle, with a 'Zcash flips Bitcoin' narrative that could send Zcash to five figures such as $20K, alongside Hyperliquid flipping BNB.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Defines the narrative-reflexivity upside case; he owns both ZEC and HYPE to express it.
insights.quote: the Zcash trade relative to Bitcoin over the next couple of years, it's going to closely resemble the salon trade relative to Ethereum from last cycle

insights.claim: Maeda reads strength in the Zcash/Bitcoin monthly chart, Pearl, Monero and Zama as market signals that alternate stores of value and privacy assets are getting a bid, though he does not own Pearl, Monero or Zama.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Breadth across privacy/alt-SoV names supports a sector theme rather than a single-coin pump.
insights.quote: alternate stores of values and privacy assets are getting a bid

insights.claim: Pearl, which ran from about 30–40 cents in the summer to close to $3, is built on the thesis that Bitcoin is a net AI loser as unprofitable miners pivot to AI inference, while Pearl can be mined by GPUs also used for AI.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Miner pivot to AI is a potential threat to Bitcoin hash rate/security; watch hash-rate trends.
insights.quote: Bitcoin is a net AI loser because Bitcoin miners are becoming unprofitable

insights.claim: Maeda frames Zcash as having a second-mover advantage over Bitcoin, analogous to Facebook over MySpace and Google over Yahoo, offering privacy, scalability and quantum resistance as the next evolution after Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Core long-term bull framework: incumbency in crypto may not be permanent.
insights.quote: Zcash offers the second mover advantage where Bitcoin proved the market

themes.theme: Macro crypto liquidity, sentiment and perp DEX strategy

insights.claim: Maeda flags that stablecoin market cap has started declining, which is bearish because most coins are worthless and inflationary, so dollars leaving the ecosystem push the average coin lower; he cites the Binance hack and North Korea-linked exploits as possible drivers.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Monitor stablecoin supply as a liquidity gauge for alt exposure; contraction argues for staying defensive.
insights.quote: if the amount of dollars is leaving the ecosystem, then the average coin will just have to go down in price

insights.claim: Maeda believes perp DEXs will keep growing and the best plays are owning HYPE, Lighter or Variational and farming new perp DEX airdrops, noting that skeptics declared perp farming over after Hyperliquid and again after Lighter.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Ongoing airdrop farming opportunity; Variational's token/airdrop expected next month is a near-term catalyst.
insights.quote: They said this after lighter variational I think will be a major cook.

insights.claim: Maeda says crypto sentiment is very bad and partly justified by political grifting, crushed hopes, and meme-coin rugs, and expects most crypto to go to zero while a few names like Zcash and perp DEX coins produce outsized returns.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Advocates concentration in a few high-conviction assets rather than broad alt beta.
insights.quote: most crypto is going to zero, right? Similar to how most stocks and most startups go to zero.

insights.claim: After large wins or losses Maeda takes a 'dopamine detox' of at least a week to avoid ego-driven sloppy trades, citing past detoxes after closing his ETH short and after selling the Zcash bottom in June before buying back more.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Behavioral risk control: biggest losses often follow biggest wins.
insights.quote: people's biggest losses often follow their biggest wins or biggest losses
